content.summary: Create ground-truth segmentation masks for training machine learning models. Paint annotations directly on your images using brush and eraser tools.
content.body:
The Quick Annotation Tool provides a browser-based painting interface for creating segmentation masks on TIFF image stacks. These annotations serve as ground truth for training U-Net segmentation models.

Key Features:
• Multi-class support with color-coded labels
• Brush and eraser tools with adjustable size
• Full undo/redo history for each slice
• Autosave to prevent data loss
• Resume unfinished work or edit existing annotations

Workflow:
1. Select Source Image: Choose a TIFF stack to annotate
2. Annotate: Paint labels on each slice using the brush tool
3. Save: Create a final annotation file or save progress for later

The resulting annotation file can be used directly with the U-Net Segmentation module for training.

content.summary: Select the image stack you want to annotate. You can start fresh, resume unfinished work, or edit an existing annotation.
content.body:
Data Sources:
• Workspace Files: Upload or select TIFF stacks from your workspace
• Unfinished Annotations: Resume previously saved work in progress
• Existing Annotations: Edit a completed annotation (creates a new version)

File Requirements:
• Format: Multi-page TIFF (.tif, .tiff)
• Bit Depth: 8-bit or 16-bit grayscale
• Dimensions: Any size (very large files may affect performance)

Workflow Options:
• New Annotation: Start from a raw image with no existing labels
• Resume: Continue working on a previously saved unfinished annotation
• Edit: Load an existing annotation to make modifications (saves as new file)

content.summary: Use the brush to paint annotations and the eraser to remove them. Keyboard shortcuts provide quick access.
content.body:
Available Tools:

Brush (B)
Paints with the currently selected class color. Click and drag to draw continuous strokes. The brush respects the current brush size setting.

Eraser (E)
Removes annotations by painting with transparent (background). Useful for correcting mistakes or refining boundaries.

Keyboard Shortcuts:
• B - Switch to brush tool
• E - Switch to eraser tool
• [ - Decrease brush size
• ] - Increase brush size
• Ctrl+Z - Undo last stroke
• Ctrl+Y - Redo undone stroke
• Left/Right arrows - Navigate between slices

content.summary: Adjust the brush diameter for precise or broad strokes. Use the slider or keyboard shortcuts.
content.body:
The brush size slider controls the diameter of both the brush and eraser tools in pixels.

Small sizes (1-10px): Precise work on boundaries and fine details
Medium sizes (10-25px): General annotation work
Large sizes (25-50px): Quickly filling large regions

Keyboard Shortcuts:
• [ - Decrease brush size by 5px
• ] - Increase brush size by 5px

The brush preview follows your cursor, showing exactly where paint will be applied.

content.summary: Undo and redo strokes on each slice. Autosave protects your work from accidental loss.
content.body:
Undo/Redo:
Each slice maintains its own history stack. Use undo to revert the last brush stroke, and redo to restore it.

• Undo (Ctrl+Z): Reverts the most recent stroke on the current slice
• Redo (Ctrl+Y): Restores a previously undone stroke
• History is per-slice: changing slices doesn't affect undo/redo state

Autosave:
When enabled, your work is automatically saved every 2 minutes if changes have been made. This protects against browser crashes or accidental navigation.

• Toggle autosave on/off using the switch in the History section
• The status indicator shows when autosave is in progress
• Manual saves are still available via the "Save Progress" button

content.summary: Define multiple classes for different structures in your images. Each class has a unique color and label.
content.body:
Classes represent different categories of structures you want to segment. For example:
• Class 1: Cell membrane
• Class 2: Nucleus
• Class 3: Background organelles

Managing Classes:
• Add Class (+): Creates a new class with an auto-assigned color
• Select Class: Click a class to make it active for painting
• Toggle Visibility: Hide/show annotations of a specific class
• Delete Class: Remove a class and all its annotations

Class Colors:
Each class is assigned a distinct color for visibility. Colors are chosen automatically to maximize contrast between classes.

Best Practices:
• Create all needed classes before starting to annotate
• Use consistent class assignments across all slices
• The active class is highlighted in the class list

annotation.definition: A labeled mask where each pixel is assigned to a class (background or object categories)

ground-truth.definition: Human-created labels that represent the correct answer, used to train and evaluate machine learning models

class.definition: A category of pixels in a segmentation task, such as 'cell', 'background', or 'nucleus'

mask.definition: An image where pixel values represent class labels rather than visual intensity

brush.definition: A painting tool that applies the current class label to pixels as you draw
